bibl.title: Extensive sequencing of seven human genomes to characterize benchmark reference materials

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: SEVEN HUMAN GENOMES SEQUENCED TWELVE WAYS TO BECOME THE THING OTHER METHODS ARE JUDGED AGAINST - NIST Reference Materials, distributed as DNA in vials, against which anyone can benchmark the accuracy of their variant calls
span.quote: Reference Materials act to calibrate, benchmark, or validate a measurement process. These samples are often the source of the scales on which we report our results (e.g., the Molar concentration of cholesterol), and they can be a physical realization of the SI units. Our ability to compare results between laboratories in most applications depends on Reference Materials.

span.label: what data are needed to characterize a human genome well enough that it can serve as a physical standard of correctness for sequencing
span.quote: The Genome in a Bottle Consortium has formed an Analysis Team to coordinate analyses by groups that are interested in analyzing these data. The primary goal of this group is to establish high-confidence phased variant calls of all sizes for these genomes, so that anyone can benchmark accuracy of their calls for these genomes.

span.label: a public data set from 12 sequencing technologies across seven genomes - five current or candidate NIST Reference Materials - with per-technology methods and technical validation
span.quote: The data come from 12 technologies: BioNano Genomics, Complete Genomics paired-end and LFR, Ion Proton exome, Oxford Nanopore, Pacific Biosciences, SOLiD, 10X Genomics GemCode WGS, and Illumina exome and WGS paired-end, mate-pair, and synthetic long reads.

span.label: method
span.quote: The data come from 12 technologies: BioNano Genomics, Complete Genomics paired-end and LFR, Ion Proton exome, Oxford Nanopore, Pacific Biosciences, SOLiD, 10X Genomics GemCode WGS, and Illumina exome and WGS paired-end, mate-pair, and synthetic long reads.

span.label: correctness as something manufactured, characterised and shipped, rather than argued for
span.quote: Reference Materials act to calibrate, benchmark, or validate a measurement process. These samples are often the source of the scales on which we report our results (e.g., the Molar concentration of cholesterol), and they can be a physical realization of the SI units. Our ability to compare results between laboratories in most applications depends on Reference Materials.

span.label: description of a reference material and its characterisation: 12 sequencing and mapping technologies applied to the same DNA, each with its own library preparation, pipeline and per-technology validation statistics
span.term: description of a reference material and its characterisation: 12 sequencing and mapping technologies applied to the same DNA, each with its own library preparation, pipeline and per-technology validation statistics
span.quote: The NIST Reference Material DNA has been characterized to an unprecedented degree. We have collected a large diverse set of data from 12 sequencing technologies and library preparation methods ( Table 1 ). These data include high-depth paired-end short read whole genome sequencing (WGS) and whole exome sequencing (WES), long mate-pair WGS, pseudo long read (‘read clouds’) WGS, long read WGS, genome mapping, and exome sequencing.

span.label: A REFERENCE MATERIAL IS AN OPERATIONAL DEFINITION OF `CORRECT` THAT SHIPS IN A VIAL: `Reference Materials act to CALIBRATE, BENCHMARK, OR VALIDATE a measurement process. These samples are often THE SOURCE OF THE SCALES ON WHICH WE REPORT OUR RESULTS (e.g., the Molar concentration of cholesterol), and they can be A PHYSICAL REALIZATION OF THE SI UNITS. Our ability to COMPARE RESULTS BETWEEN LABORATORIES in most applications DEPENDS ON REFERENCE MATERIALS`
span.quote: Reference Materials act to calibrate, benchmark, or validate a measurement process. These samples are often the source of the scales on which we report our results (e.g., the Molar concentration of cholesterol), and they can be a physical realization of the SI units. Our ability to compare results between laboratories in most applications depends on Reference Materials.

span.label: AND THE CIRCULARITY IS NAMED AS A VIRTUE: `In A VIRTUOUS CYCLE, EXISTING METHODS ARE OPTIMIZED AND NEW METHODS ARE DEVELOPED USING REFERENCE MATERIALS AS THE BENCHMARKS`. The benchmark defines what counts as correct and the methods are then tuned against it. This corpus calls that loop a trap; metrology calls it a virtuous cycle. BOTH ARE RIGHT, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WHETHER THE BENCHMARK WAS BUILT INDEPENDENTLY OF THE METHODS IT WILL JUDGE - which here it was, from twelve technologies at once
span.quote: There is a tradition of innovation in measurement science to characterize these high-impact samples 1 . New technologies are used, rigorous experimental designs are employed, and exotic methods applied 2 , 3 . In a virtuous cycle, existing methods are optimized and new methods are developed using reference materials as the benchmarks.

span.label: AND TWO ALIGNERS READING THE SAME MOLECULE DISAGREE ABOUT WHAT KIND OF THING A VARIANT IS: `The proportion of mismatches to indels was similar for both aligners, however BWA ANNOTATES INDELS PREFERENTIALLY AS DELETIONS, AND GraphMap FAVORS INSERTIONS`. Not how much difference - WHAT KIND. Insertion or deletion is a property of the tool here, not of the DNA
span.quote: GraphMap maps more reads than BWA MEM ont2d, which cover a greater region of the genome ( Table 13 ), and allows a higher error rate ( Table 14 ). The proportion of mismatches to indels was similar for both aligners, however BWA annotates indels preferentially as deletions, and GraphMap favors insertions.

span.label: and the paper draws the conclusion itself: `This highlights THE IMPORTANCE OF THE CHOICE OF ALIGNER and that overall quality of the reads and nature of analysis may be useful to consider PRIOR TO CHOOSING ONE OVER THE OTHER`
span.quote: This highlights the importance of the choice of aligner and that overall quality of the reads and nature of analysis may be useful to consider prior to choosing one over the other.

span.label: AND THE METRIC WAS CHANGED BECAUSE THE FIRST ONE MEASURED THE WRONG THING, WITH THE REASON GIVEN: `The high rate of PCR duplicates (close to 50% in some libraries) RESULTED IN LOWER THAN EXPECTED SEQUENCE COVERAGE ... A MORE RELEVANT METRIC for mate-pair data is THE PHYSICAL COVERAGE, which measures the number of inferred fragments that cover a particular genomic position`. A defensible substitution, made in the open, after the first number looked bad
span.quote: The high rate of PCR duplicates (close to 50% in some libraries) resulted in lower than expected sequence coverage (13–17x average across all sequenced genomic positions). A more relevant metric for mate-pair data is the physical coverage, which measures the number of inferred fragments that cover a particular genomic position (including both the sequenced ends as well as the unsequenced genomic region between the ends).

span.label: THE REFERENCE MATERIAL IS NOT IDENTICAL TO ITSELF: `It is possible that SMALL DIFFERENCES MAY EXIST between the NIST RM DNA and the DNA from Coriell because they come from DIFFERENT PASSAGES OF CELLS and may contain DIFFERENT NEW MUTATIONS`. The standard of correctness has batch variation, stated by the people who make it
span.quote: It is possible that small differences may exist between the NIST RM DNA and the DNA from Coriell because they come from different passages of cells and may contain different new mutations.

span.label: AND THE REFERENCE FOR `THE HUMAN GENOME` IS THREE ANCESTRIES, NAMED: `The pilot genome (NIST RM 8398) is an oft-used genome of CAUCASIAN ANCESTRY: NA12878 from the CEPH Utah Reference Collection. In addition, genomes from two family trios ... one of ASHKENAZI JEWISH (AJ) ancestry and the other of HAN CHINESE ancestry`. Whose genome is the standard is a decision, and this one is recorded
span.quote: The pilot genome (NIST RM 8398) is an oft-used genome of Caucasian ancestry: NA12878 from the CEPH Utah Reference Collection. In addition, genomes from two family trios (both Mother-Father-Son) have been selected from the Personal Genomes Project (PGP), one of Ashkenazi Jewish (AJ) ancestry and the other of Han Chinese ancestry.

span.label: and the standard is also a commercial input: the PGP samples `are CONSENTED MORE BROADLY for many applications, INCLUDING COMMERCIAL REDISTRIBUTION`, and `there are ALREADY THREE COMMERCIAL PRODUCTS from the same cell lines from which the NIST Reference Material DNA is prepared`
span.quote: The samples from PGP are consented more broadly for many applications, including commercial redistribution. There are already three commercial products from the same cell lines from which the NIST Reference Material DNA is prepared: AcroMetrix Oncology Hotspot Control from Thermo Fisher Scientific, GIAB HDx Reference Standards from Horizon Diagnostics, and cell line DNA with synthetic DNA spike-ins from SeraCare Life Sciences.

span.label: THE STAGED BODY CARRIES DAMAGE THAT HAPPENED AT THE PUBLISHER, NOT IN OUR EXTRACTION. It reads `very low (2X coverage (at least 650 Kb for either dataset, with either mapper)` - an unbalanced parenthesis where `<2X` belonged. THE SAME TEXT IS IN EUROPE PMC's OWN fullTextXML, checked directly: an unescaped `<` deleted itself and the text up to the next `>` before we ever fetched the file. Every shape in NOTES/EXTRACTION_DAMAGE_TAXONOMY.md happens during OUR extraction; this one did not
